question.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{3} & \frac{2}{3} \\ \frac{2}{3} & \frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ given above. Which of the following statements are true?

I. ${A}^{T}=A$

II. ${A}^{2}=A$

III. $A$ is an orthogonal projection matrix
question.worked_solution:
Recall that $Q$ is an orthogonal projection matrix if and only if ${Q}^{2}=Q$ and ${Q}^{T}=Q.$ 

With that in mind, let's examine each of the statements in turn.

- Statement I is true. Indeed, ${A}^{T}=A.$

- Statement II is false. Indeed, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{2} & =A\cdot A \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{3} & \frac{2}{3} \\ \frac{2}{3} & \frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{3} & \frac{2}{3} \\ \frac{2}{3} & \frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}4 & 2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}4 & 2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{9}[\begin{aligned}4 & 2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 & 2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{9}[\begin{aligned}20 & 10 \\ 10 & 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{20}{9} & \frac{10}{9} \\ \frac{10}{9} & \frac{5}{9}\end{aligned}] \\  & \ne A.\end{aligned}
$$

- Statement III is false since not both statements I and II are true.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only."
